title: Flat schematic closure of a generic subgroup over a DVR
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $K$, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme is an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams; a homomorphism respects these operations. Let $G$ be a separated $S$-group scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with no flatness hypothesis on $G$. Let $H_K\hookrightarrow G_K$ be a closed subgroup scheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], where subscript $K$ denotes base change [def-pc-base-change]. Define $C\hookrightarrow G$ to be the schematic closure of $H_K$: on each affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq G$ its ideal is
$$I_V=\ker\bigl(B\longrightarrow\Gamma(V\times_G H_K,\mathcal O_{H_K})\bigr).$$
These ideals define a closed subscheme $C$, with $C_K=H_K$ as closed subschemes of $G_K$. The operations of $G$ restrict to $C$, making it a separated flat $S$-group scheme of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Moreover, for every flat $S$-scheme $X$ and every $S$-morphism $v:X\to G$ whose generic base change $v_K$ factors through $H_K$, there is a unique factorization $X\to C\hookrightarrow G$.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.5, proof, printed p.166, schematic closure paragraph. Kernel construction and flat-source factorization made explicit; source read online, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: For an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $G$, write $B_K=B\otimes_RK$ and let $J_V\subseteq B_K$ define $H_K\cap V_K$. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [def-weil-closed-immersion] identify $V\times_GH_K$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B_K/J_V)$. Thus the stated ideal is $I_V=\{b\in B:b/1\in J_V\}$. This construction commutes with localization in $B$: for a multiplicative subset $T$, an element $b/t$ maps to zero in $T^{-1}(B_K/J_V)$ exactly when $ub/1\in J_V$ for some $u\in T$, equivalently $ub\in I_V$. Hence the new kernel is $T^{-1}I_V$. The ideals $J_V$ are the restrictions of the given closed-subgroup ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; the calculation on principal opens therefore makes the $I_V$ compatible on every overlap, checked on a principal-open refinement. They define a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf (locally the ideal associated to $I_V$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme] to obtain a closed subscheme $i:C\hookrightarrow G$ with affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}(B/I_V)$ and exactly the ideals in the statement.

proof.text: After inverting $R\setminus\{0\}$, the ideal generated by $I_V$ is $J_V$. Indeed every element of $J_V\subset B_K$ can be written $b/r$ with $0\ne r\in R$; then $b/1=r(b/r)\in J_V$, so $b\in I_V$. The reverse inclusion follows from the definition. Consequently $(B/I_V)\otimes_RK=B_K/J_V$. These identifications commute with restrictions by step 1, and the affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] shows that $C_K=H_K$ as closed subschemes of $G_K$, with their given inclusions.

source.place: Tag 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image); elementary extension/contraction calculation for a localization

proof.text: The kernel description gives an injection $B/I_V\hookrightarrow B_K/J_V$ of $R$-modules. The target is a $K$-vector space, so multiplication by every $0\ne r\in R$ is injective there and therefore on $B/I_V$. A DVR is a principal ideal domain [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] makes $B/I_V$ flat over $R$. Apply [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-local-criterion] with $A=M=B/I_V$: at every point of this chart its local ring is flat over the appropriate local ring of $R$. The charts cover $C$, so the stalk definition [def-weil-flat-morphism] gives flatness of $C\to S$. Only the quotient $B/I_V$ was shown to inject into its generic localization; no injectivity of $B\to B_K$, and no flatness of $G$, has been assumed.

We first prove the factorization assertion, without using a group structure on $C$. Let $v:X\to G$ satisfy its hypotheses. For $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset G$, cover $v^{-1}V$ by affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}D$. Since $X/S$ is flat, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] gives flatness of $D$ over $R$, and [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] gives $R$-torsion-freeness. If $b\in I_V$, its image $d\in D$ vanishes in $D\otimes_RK$: the assumed generic factorization through $H_K$ annihilates $b/1\in J_V$. The fraction criterion says some $0\ne r\in R$ has $rd=0$; torsion-freeness gives $d=0$. Thus $B\to D$ factors uniquely through $B/I_V$, defining a lift $W\to C$. On overlaps the lifts coincide: a map into a closed subscheme is determined uniquely by the composite into $G$, since its local ring maps factor through quotient rings [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Hence these local maps glue to a unique $X\to C$. This also proves that $i$ is a monomorphism for arbitrary test schemes, a fact used below. Neither quasi-compactness nor separatedness of $X$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0538 (lemma-flat-torsion-free); morphisms.tex Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize); explicit denominator argument expanding Conrad Theorem 5.3.5, printed p.166

proof.text: The scheme $C\times_SC$ is flat over $S$. Indeed it is covered by the affine products of the charts $\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\operatorname{Spec}D$ of $C$; these products are $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RD)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Both modules $A,D$ are $R$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. For an injective $R$-module map $N\to P$, tensor first with $A$ and then with $D$; both maps remain injective by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Rebracketing $((n\otimes a)\otimes d)\mapsto n\otimes(a\otimes d)$, with the inverse on pure tensors, identifies the composite with tensoring $N\to P$ by $A\otimes_RD$. Thus this ring is $R$-flat. The affine local criterion [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-local-criterion] gives flat stalks on the product charts, and [def-weil-flat-morphism] gives the assertion. Also $S/S$ is flat: tensoring with $R$ is the identity.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); elementary tensor argument from flatness; algebra.tex Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization)

proof.text: Apply the factorization proved in step 4 to the maps $m_G\circ(i\times i):C\times_SC\to G$, $\operatorname{inv}_G\circ i:C\to G$, and $e_G:S\to G$. Their sources are flat by steps 3 and 5. By step 2 their generic maps are the multiplication, inverse and identity maps of the given closed subgroup $H_K$, followed by its inclusion, so all factor through $H_K$. We obtain $m_C$, $\operatorname{inv}_C$, and $e_C$ with composites into $G$ equal to those displayed maps. Associativity is checked by composing both maps from $C\times_SC\times_SC$ to $C$ with $i$; they become the two equal associative products in $G$. Cancellation of the monomorphism $i$, proved in step 4, gives equality in $C$. The two unit and the two inverse diagrams follow by the same cancellation, respectively from the unit and inverse diagrams in $G$. Thus these are actual restricted operations defining an $S$-group, and $i$ is a homomorphism. This is an application of the already proved factorization, not an appeal to schematic density of an unproved product.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.5 proof, printed p.166, schematic closure paragraph; explicit assembly from steps 2--5

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover $G=\bigcup_a\operatorname{Spec}B_a$ with each $B_a$ finite type over $R$, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its inverse images in $C$ are the affine quotients $\operatorname{Spec}(B_a/I_a)$, so give a finite affine cover with finite type coordinate algebras: the images of generators of $B_a$ generate $B_a/I_a$. Hence $C/S$ is of finite type. It is separated as well. The square formed by $\Delta_C$, $\Delta_G$, $i$ and $i\times i$ is cartesian: for maps into $C$, equality of their images in $G$ implies equality by the monomorphism property in step 4. A base change of a closed immersion is closed: on affine charts it is the quotient map $D\to D\otimes_B(B/J)=D/JD$, by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $\Delta_C$ is closed because $\Delta_G$ is closed, and [def-weil-proper-morphism] gives separatedness. The construction is local on the target, so this argument does not require any whole group scheme to be affine. Finally [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] gives quasi-separatedness of $C/S$.

source.place: Tags 01KK (definition-separated), 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme), 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); elementary quotient generators and cartesian diagonal argument

proof.text: Every ideal of the DVR $R$ is principal [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], hence finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Each $B_a/I_a$ of step 7 is a finite type $R$-algebra, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes it finitely presented over $R$. Thus $C/S$ is locally of finite presentation. The finite affine cover gives quasi-compactness, and step 7 gives quasi-separatedness; these three conditions are finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Together with the construction, generic-fibre equality, flatness, group operations, and factorization in steps 1--6, this proves every clause of the item.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q98-13ff3f3ce (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full: an 8-step first split with no new nodes, the statement unchanged from the base, and no repair note. I read all 21 cited statements. The statement is correct: it is the flat closure of a generic subgroup over a DVR with no flatness on G. I tested it on R[x]/(πx), where C is the zero section; on α_p, where C = Spec R[x]/(x^p); on the case G flat with H_K = G_K, where C = G; and on a non-flat X, a counterexample showing why the flatness hypothesis on X is needed. Steps 1-2: the kernel description, its compatibility with localization, J_V = I_V·B_K and C_K = H_K all check from the affine fibre product, the closed-immersion and ideal-sheaf nodes, and the quasi-coherent-ideal lemma. Step 3: the quotient is torsion-free because it injects into a K-vector space, so it is flat by the PID lemma (0AUW), and stalks are flat by 00HT(6), which I checked at algebra.tex lines 9212-9216. Step 4: flat sources factor, using 01U5, flat-implies-torsion-free and the monomorphism property of a closed immersion. Step 5: C×_S C is flat by double tensoring, then 00HT(6). Step 6: the group operations come from factorization and cancellation of the monomorphism. Step 7: finite type, plus separatedness because the diagonal square is cartesian and closed immersions are stable under base change. Step 8: finite presentation via 00FP. Small gap, not counted as a fault: step 7 does not spell out finite type over the other affine open Spec K of S. The batch-5 flag on lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain is accepted: it is a Mathlib leaf (Module.Flat.torsion_eq_bot), pure commutative algebra, not part of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proofs, it adds nothing to the batch-5 closure, and no non-trf node states it. The declared tool use lem-pc-affine-flat-module-local-criterion (generic 00HT(6)) is accepted. No duplicate of the item exists in the DAG, and no SGA source is used. Conrad Theorem 5.3.5 is not in the local literature (WANTED), so I checked the mathematics against Stacks instead. No changes.
